newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says Buba revaluation no effect on 97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says Buba revaluation no effect on 97 budget.

text.p: A leading member of Chancellor Helmut's Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) said on Tuesday the revaluation of the Bundesbank's gold and currency reserves would begin this year but have no effect on the 1997 budget.

"The revaluation of gold and currency reserves will begin in steps in 1997 and therefore have no effect for (the) 1997 (budget)," Wolfgang Schaueble, CDU parliamentary leader told journalists after a party meeting to discuss the plan in Bonn.

Schaeuble said talks between the government and the Bundesbank over the controversial revaluation of Bundesbank assets were proceeding well and said members of the CDU and Bavarian sister party the Christian Social Union (CSU) had reacted well to the results of their discussions.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer earlier held a meeting to try and reach agreement on Bonn's plans which the powerful bank had strongly criticised.
Head of the CSU parliamentary group Michael Glos said members of both parties would reject a parliamentary motion due to be brought by opposition parties calling for Waigel's dismissal over the plan.
